status_legend.DETERMINISTIC_TESTED: Repository-local deterministic tests pass without paid model calls.
status_legend.LIVE_ACCEPTED: Merged production path has passed a real Issue/Actions acceptance test.
status_legend.OPERATIONAL: Depends on GitHub or a manual platform operation and cannot be made fully autonomous inside the current minimum-permission boundary.

p0.name: failed-task-resubmission
p0.implementation: Duplicate detection blocks open, running, completed and duplicate predecessors, but does not allow failed/not_planned history to poison a new Issue fingerprint.
p0.production_acceptance: Governance Issue 84 repeated failed Issue 79 exactly, received new task_id gov-84-expert and a new child Issue rather than CONTROL_DUPLICATE.

p0.name: comment-pagination
p0.implementation: Governance child monitoring, retry accounting and status ownership checks scan up to ten pages of 100 comments.

p0.name: task-id-binding
p0.implementation: Production monitoring accepts only an exact governance-generated task_id. A bot terminal with a missing or mismatched Task ID is provisional evidence and polling continues for a later task-bound terminal; it is never accepted as the result.
p0.production_acceptance: Governance Issue 84 stayed open after an unbound primary rejection and completed only after the task-bound gov-84-expert fallback rejection arrived.

p0.name: artifact-contract
p0.implementation: Compute/API success requires Artifact ID, 64-hex digest and matching URL. Expert success additionally requires primary and final-attestation Artifact identities. An incomplete success receipt is provisional and monitoring continues for a corrected audited receipt.
p0.production_acceptance: Compute governance Issue 78 passed with a task-bound Artifact identity; intelligence and paid expert success are not required for this zero-call release.

p0.name: late-terminal-reconciliation
p0.implementation: A serialized scheduled/closed-Issue worker reconciles only owner-authored canonical [control] timeout or monitor-error records. It derives task_id from the governance Issue number, enforces the route-fixed child repository and reuses provisional terminal validation.

p0.name: lost-trigger-recovery
p0.implementation: When no trusted child bot activity is observed, governance performs at most one marker-bound recovery: close/reopen for compute/API or one exact expert command repost.

p0.name: gpts-trusted-comment-read
p0.implementation: Repository OpenAPI exposes one additional read-only governance Issue comments operation. No child-repository or mutation operation is exposed.
p0.operational_boundary: A custom GPT does not automatically import a changed repository OpenAPI file; the GPT Action schema must be updated in the GPT configuration before live acceptance.

p0.name: json-complexity-and-secret-variants
p0.implementation: The gateway bounds body size, JSON depth, node count, key length and string length, and rejects camelCase authorization/secret variants plus executable field names.

p1_required: GitHub rate-limit aware backoff using Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Reset
bounded retry and explicit receipt for next-worker wake failure
daily token scope and repository identity health check
standard user-facing status dictionary and next-action text
long-term Issue and Artifact archive policy
operational_boundaries: GitHub platform-wide outages cannot be bypassed without violating the evidence architecture.
Closing an Issue does not cancel an already-running child workflow because the control token intentionally has no Actions write permission.
Exact hidden fine-grained PAT settings for the custom GPT cannot be read back through repository APIs.
The updated OpenAPI file must be imported into the custom GPT before the new read-only comments operation is available there.
